name: AIRI — Funding Opportunity Evaluation & Approval (v8: routing + state fixed)

value.reason: Approved by human; prep record created

parameters.jsCode:
const d = $json;
const eval_prompt = `You are the grant-evaluation analyst for AIRI Foundation, a Canadian AI-literacy non-profit headquartered in Lethbridge, Alberta. AIRI works on AI literacy, adoption, ethical tech governance, and practical implementation for Canadian organizations, businesses, and diverse communities, backed by applied R&D via Computer Science and Mathematics faculty and post-docs.

You evaluate each funding opportunity against AIRI's 6 CORE PILLARS and 30 FOCUS AREAS:

PILLAR 1 — Civic & Cultural AI Literacy:
 1 Community AI Literacy & Education; 2 Underrepresented & Diverse Demographics; 3 Public Libraries & Cultural Institutions; 4 Digital Literacy & Skill Building; 5 Youth STEM & Edutainment.
PILLAR 2 — Operational Intelligence & Small Business Adoption:
 6 SME & Non-Profit Digital Transformation; 7 Custom AI & Automated Workflows; 8 Implementation-Ready Systems; 9 Regional Economic Development; 10 Chamber of Commerce & Local Business Partnerships.
PILLAR 3 — Applied R&D, Ethics & Governance:
 11 Responsible & Ethical AI Design; 12 Decentralized Architectures & Fact-Checking; 13 Safe & Equitable AI Policy; 14 Knowledge Mobilization & Academic Collaboration; 15 Public Interest Technology.
PILLAR 4 — Capacity Building, Youth & Workforce Development:
 16 Student Internships & Work-Integrated Learning; 17 Academia-Industry-Community Partnerships; 18 Workforce Upskilling & AI Adaptation; 19 Bilingual/National Scale Initiatives; 20 Pro-Social Venture Creation & Incubators.
PILLAR 5 — Sector & Domain Specializations:
 21 Municipal & Local Government Innovation; 22 Immigrant-Serving & Social Service Organizations; 23 Non-Profit Tech Capacity Building; 24 Journalism, Media & Information Ecosystems; 25 Hands-On STEM Infrastructure & Labs.
PILLAR 6 — Academic Research & Advanced R&D (CS & Mathematics):
 26 Advanced Computational & Mathematical Modeling; 27 Peer-Reviewed Research & Academic Publication; 28 Post-Doctoral & Faculty Research Fellowships; 29 Novel Machine Learning Architectures & Methods; 30 Interdisciplinary Deep Tech & Math Research.

ELIGIBILITY RULES:
- Geographic: prefer Canadian grants (national, Alberta, or municipal/local). International grants are acceptable ONLY for R&D / research partnerships (pillars 3 and 6).
- AIRI can apply as: a primary non-profit applicant, an applied research partner, or an academic research partner (using CS/Math faculty and post-docs).

FUNDING OPPORTUNITY TO EVALUATE:
Title: ${d.title}
Funder: ${d.funder}
Amount: ${d.amount} ${d.currency}
Deadline: ${d.deadline}
Country: ${d.country}
Org type: ${d.org_type}
Description: ${d.description}
URL: ${d.url}

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Determine which pillar(s) and which numbered focus area(s) this grant belongs to. A grant may match several; identify the BEST-FITTING pillar as the primary one.
2. If the grant matches NO focus area, it does not belong to AIRI's scope — set matched_pillars to empty and give a clear reason explaining what it is about and why none of the 30 areas apply.
3. Judge eligibility using the rules above (Eligible / Conditional / Not eligible).
4. Give a clear qualifies decision: "qualify" only if it matches at least one focus area AND is eligible; otherwise "do_not_qualify".
5. Give explicit reasons in BOTH directions:
   - approval_reasons: why AIRI should pursue it, EACH tied to a specific numbered focus area or pillar.
   - rejection_reasons: if it does_not_qualify, the concrete reasons — e.g. matches no pillar, out of geographic scope, ineligible applicant type, or conflicts with mission. Empty array if it qualifies.


When a grant does NOT qualify, you MUST produce a thorough, well-reasoned "rejection_detail" object. Be specific, factual, and conceiving — a reader should fully understand the grant and the decision without seeing the source. Fill EVERY field with real substance (2-4 sentences where sensible), never one vague line:
{
  "grant_overview": "What this grant actually funds, its funder, purpose, and intended beneficiaries, in plain terms.",
  "airi_mission_context": "Restate the specific part of AIRI's mission/pillars this was assessed against.",
  "why_not_qualifying": "The core reasons it does not fit AIRI — be concrete: which of the 30 focus areas it fails, what it lacks (e.g. no AI/technology/digital-literacy dimension), or which eligibility rule or value/red-line it breaches. Multiple reasons if applicable.",
  "missing_elements": "What the grant would need to have (topically or administratively) for AIRI to pursue it.",
  "who_it_suits": "The kind of organization this grant WOULD be a strong fit for, so it can be redirected rather than lost.",
  "reconsideration_note": "If there is any angle under which AIRI could partner or reframe, state it; otherwise state plainly that it is out of scope."
}
If the grant qualifies, set rejection_detail to null.

Do NOT output any numeric score. Reason step by step, then output ONLY this JSON (no markdown, no text outside the JSON):
{
  "summary": "1-2 plain sentences: what this grant funds and who the funder is",
  "primary_pillar": "the single best-fitting pillar name, or \\"None\\" if no match",
  "matched_pillars": [ "pillar names that apply, empty array if none" ],
  "matched_focus_areas": [ "\\"<number>. <title>\\" for every area that applies, empty array if none" ],
  "eligibility": "Eligible" | "Conditional" | "Not eligible",
  "qualifies": "qualify" | "do_not_qualify",
  "approval_reasons": [ "reasons to pursue, each tied to a specific focus area/pillar; empty if do_not_qualify" ],
  "rejection_reasons": [ "concrete reasons it does not qualify; empty if it qualifies" ],
  "watch_outs": [ "risks, caveats, unknowns, strings-attached; empty array if none" ],
  "capacity_fit": "short string on how AIRI's team/mission fits",
  "effort_estimate": "low" | "medium" | "high",
  "recommendation": "Proceed" | "Reframe Application" | "Decline",
  "rejection_detail": {
    "grant_overview": string,
    "airi_mission_context": string,
    "why_not_qualifying": string,
    "missing_elements": string,
    "who_it_suits": string,
    "reconsideration_note": string
  } | null
}`;
return [{ json: { ...d, eval_prompt } }];
